structured.approach: BE-03 asks whether the database changes this feature needs are done. I read both contracted inputs in full (feat.tasks, feat.design) to find what TSK-05 and TSK-06 in ap_aging need for storage. Then I checked the ap_aging checkout. I listed its files with Glob, searched them for database and migration terms with Grep, and read aging.py and __init__.py. The step hook does not allow shell commands, so I used only file tools. The design and the repository agree that the feature has no storage and needs no migration, so the output records that no database change is required, that none is pending, and when this check should be run again.

claims.text: The design lists 'Storage, database, schema migration' as out of scope; the data in scope is in-memory records, delay history, risk map, overdue rows and CT-1 JSON.
Design decision DD-1 adds no new repository, service, runtime, library or storage, and NF-10 requires every new function to be pure and in-memory with no I/O.
The Backend tasks TSK-05 and TSK-06 change only src/ap_aging/aging.py, src/ap_aging/__init__.py and tests/test_overdue.py; no schema or migration file is in their budget.
ap_aging has no database; no migrations exist or are required.
aging.py imports only datetime.date, decimal.Decimal and typing, and aging_buckets works on an in-memory iterable of invoice dicts; the package version is 1.4.0.
ap_aging is Python 3.9 using the standard library.
Adding a transport between ap_aging and ap_portal, or any storage or network call from the libraries, would reopen DES-01 and so also this database check.
The paid_date key is added in memory by the Data Engineering lane in transform.to_model (TSK-01), not by a database change.
